candidates.title: Bibliothèque du Plateau-Mont-Royal – bébé-lecture / lapsit storytime
candidates.description: The local branch of the Réseau des bibliothèques de Montréal regularly offers gentle lap-sit and early literacy sessions for babies 0–18 months with a caregiver. A calm, free, and welcoming indoor option year-round.
candidates.coverageNote: Library branches in the Plateau reliably run newborn/infant programming; specific schedule not individually verified.

candidates.title: CLSC du Plateau-Mont-Royal – parent-newborn drop-in support group
candidates.description: Montreal CLSCs serve as community health anchors and routinely host drop-in new-parent groups (groupes de parents) where caregivers with newborns can meet, ask questions, and connect. Free and walk-in friendly.
candidates.coverageNote: CLSC-run newborn support groups are standard across Montreal neighbourhoods; current schedule at this specific CLSC not confirmed.

candidates.title: Parent-and-baby aqua-fitness / tot pool time at a nearby Ville de Montréal pool
candidates.description: Montréal municipal pools offer parent-and-infant water familiarisation classes for babies as young as 4 months. A gentle way to introduce water and connect with other new parents in the borough.
candidates.coverageNote: Parent-infant pool programs are widely available at Ville de Montréal facilities; nearest pool to the Plateau and current session dates not individually verified.

candidates.title: Parc Lafontaine – stroller walks and fresh-air outings
candidates.description: Parc Lafontaine is one of Montréal's largest green spaces, steps from the Plateau, with wide paved paths ideal for daily stroller walks. A standing free option for new parents seeking outdoor air and gentle movement any day of the week.
candidates.coverageNote: Parc Lafontaine is a well-established, publicly accessible park in the Plateau-Mont-Royal borough.

candidates.title: Café-parents or new-parent social meetup (Plateau neighbourhood)
candidates.description: Community organisations and family resource centres (Centres de ressources familiales) in the Plateau periodically host informal café-parents gatherings where caregivers bring newborns, share experiences, and ease isolation. Usually free or by donation.
candidates.coverageNote: Family resource centres operating in the Plateau are known to run these gatherings; specific current listings not confirmed.
